title: Tool generator: entity definition -> filter + full-text tool specs

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: Turns an entity into the tool specs the API/MCP expose and the executor runs. Depends on the entity schema (30.1).

background.reference: GitHub issue #309; Cole Medin: 'a tool for each attribute + a text search'.
background.includes: US-30.1 provides entity definitions. This story deterministically derives tool specs from them: one filter tool per filterable field, one full-text search tool per entity with searchable text fields. The specs are consumed by the API list endpoint, the MCP dynamic listing (US-30.5), and the executor (US-30.3).

story.i_want_to: generate a stable set of tool specs (name, description, JSON input schema) from an entity definition — filter_<entity>_by_<field> for each filterable field and search_<entity> for full-text
story.so_that: the agent tool surface is derived from schema, not hand-maintained, and every generated tool maps to an allowlisted field/operation

rationale: The generator is the bridge from declaration to surface. Making it pure and deterministic (same entity -> same specs) means the API, the MCP listing, and the executor all agree on the exact tool set and input schema, and it guarantees no tool can reference a field the entity did not mark filterable/searchable — the generator is where the executor's allowlist originates.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.ContextRetriever.ToolGenerator.specs_for/1 takes an Entity and returns a deterministic list of tool specs: one filter_<entity>_by_<field> per field where filterable == true (input: the field value + pagination), and one search_<entity> when the entity has >= 1 searchable text field (input: query string + pagination).

Each spec carries a JSON input schema typed from the field type (string/int/bool/date), a clear description, and metadata linking it to its (entity, field, operation) so the executor can dispatch without re-parsing the tool name.
Tool names are namespaced/prefixed to avoid collision with loopctl's static MCP tools (e.g. cr_filter_<entity>_by_<field>), and are stable across regenerations for an unchanged entity.
A field NOT marked filterable produces NO filter tool; an entity with no searchable field produces NO search tool — the generated surface is exactly the allowlist, nothing more.

test_cases.name: generator emits filter tools only for filterable fields + a search tool
preconditions: entity = an Entity with fields status(filterable), city(filterable), description(searchable text), secret(neither)
expected_results: specs include filter tools for status and city and a search tool; NO tool references secret; each spec carries entity/field/operation metadata + typed input schema

test_cases.name: specs are deterministic and collision-safe
steps: call specs_for/1 twice; compare names to loopctl static tool names
expected_results: identical specs both calls; generated names are prefixed and do not collide with static tool names

technical_notes: Module: Loopctl.ContextRetriever.ToolGenerator. Pure function of the entity; no DB, no side effects.
Name prefix (e.g. cr_) prevents collisions in the MCP ListTools merge (US-30.5).
The spec's (entity, field, operation) metadata is the contract the executor (US-30.3) dispatches on — do not have the executor re-parse tool names.
